# Agent & Contributor Instructions — `catalytic-register-frontiers`

**Current Build Pipeline Phase:** `P9` (Published on GitHub `v1.1.0`, Zenodo Concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.24517198`, Palomar Registry `PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004` v1, Software Heritage `swh:1:snp:f960eeda6f145e54c0ac52538ace866a16e24085`, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, and `0thernes-research-archive` `0TH-2026-010`; arXiv/HAL/external peer review in progress; tracked in `project.yaml`).  
**Governing Standards:** Build Standard for LLMs v1.2.0 (`repo.yaml`, `scripts/Audit-Repo.ps1`), Build Pipeline Models v1.0.0 (`project.yaml`, `scripts/pipeline-audit.py`), and Defensible Independent AI Research Playbook v1.3 (`docs/reviews/01-10-pass-review.md`, `docs/launch/release-checklist.md`).

Follow these repository invariants on every edit:

1. **Workspace & Shell Safety:** This repository lives on a bracketed Windows path (`Z:\[Vibe Coded (AI)]\ANTIGRAVITY\catalytic-register-frontiers`). Always use `-LiteralPath` in PowerShell file cmdlets, use `os.walk` instead of `glob.glob` in Python over bracketed paths, and run `pytest` repo-relative (`tests/test_all.py`).
2. **Zero-Mathlib Lean 4.35 Bar:** Every `.lean` file begins with `module` (14 core proof files, 8,930 lines total, max 1,511 lines; plus standalone Palomar contract files `PalomarChallenge.lean` [283 lines, zero imports, Comparator placeholder `sorry` only] and `PalomarSolution.lean` [842 lines]; 16 files / 10,055 lines total) and all proof/solution modules build with zero warnings under `autoImplicit=false`, `linter.unusedVariables=true`, `linter.deprecated=true` and zero `sorry`/`admit`/`native_decide`/custom `axiom`/`unsafe`/`@[extern]`. Every exported theorem in `Challenge.lean` / `Solution.lean` (`22` theorems `T1`, `T1a`–`T1e`, `T1s`, `T1es`, `T1sc`, `T1esc`, `T2`, `T2b`, `T3a`–`T3i`, `T4` + master conjunction) plus `Catalytic.NonVacuity.nonvac_all_hypotheses` (24 total) must pass `VerifyAxioms.lean` strictly within `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` and replay across 5 distinct locally reproducible kernel implementations in 6 runs (`lean`, `leanchecker`, `leanchecker-paranoid`, `con-leche --verified`, `con-ron --verified`, and `nanoda_bin`).
3. **Exact Arithmetic, Testing & Linters:** All computational checks in `experiments/` and `tests/` use exact integer/rational/finite-field arithmetic (`int`, `fractions.Fraction`) with no floating-point proof steps. Maintain passing Hypothesis property/metamorphic tests, mutant-killing checks, brute-force SAT encoder equivalence tests, `scripts/check_citations.py`, `ruff`, and `mypy`. Vector PDF figures must set `metadata={"CreationDate": None}`.
4. **Epistemic Integrity & Identity:** Clearly separate Tier-1..4 claims (`CLAIMS.md`, `docs/statement-fidelity.md`, `LIMITATIONS.md`). Cite primary literature (`arXiv:2609.18692`, `arXiv:2608.30238`, `doi:10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2025.6`, `doi:10.1016/j.tcs.2018.02.023`) accurately without redistributing third-party PDFs. Author is `Alexander S. Donahue` (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA; ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`; no unformed LLC claim); dual license is `Apache-2.0` (code) + `CC-BY-4.0` (prose/docs/figures).
5. **Lean Git & CI Rules (R1–R8):** Commit directly to `main`; never add git hooks, branch protection, PR templates, Dependabot, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Keep CI, lint, type, coverage, SAST, and SBOM checks report-only so they never gate commits or pushes; GitHub SLSA attestations apply to public repositories (`continue-on-error: true`). Classify every finding as exactly one of `{bug, error, issue, problem, concern, dilemma, conflict, gap, hole, blindspot}`. Regenerate LF-clean `MANIFEST.sha256` after any artifact change.
6. **Recorded N/A Tooling Decisions:**
   - *Pipeline `P5.07` (Container/Nix):* No Dockerfile or devcontainer is required because `lean/` has zero external Lake/Mathlib dependencies (pinned solely by `lean/lean-toolchain` `v4.35.0`) and Python dependencies are strictly pinned in `requirements.lock.txt`.
   - *Playbook #11 (`leanblueprint`):* Because the formalization comprises 14 self-contained zero-Mathlib modules, a static, zero-dependency theorem dependency graph and theorem-to-declaration map is published directly at `docs/index.html` (deployed via `.github/workflows/pages.yml`) instead of installing the plasTeX/Graphviz `leanblueprint` toolchain.

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0 -->
# Prime-Field Digit-Sum Dichotomy and Improved Three-Register Powering Exponents in Passive Catalytic Register Programs

[![Version 1.1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.1.0-blue.svg)](VERSION)
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.24517198.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24517198)
[![Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004](https://img.shields.io/badge/Palomar-PALOMAR--2026--11--26--000004-009E73.svg)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004&version=1)
[![Lean 4.35.0 Zero-Mathlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lean-4.35.0%20(zero--Mathlib)-brightgreen.svg)](lean/lean-toolchain)
[![5 Kernels / 6 Runs PASS](https://img.shields.io/badge/kernels-5%20impls%20%2F%206%20runs%20PASS-brightgreen.svg)](results/six_kernel_audit.txt)
[![Code License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Docs License: CC-BY-4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs%20license-CC--BY--4.0-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Status: Preprint — Not Peer Reviewed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-preprint%20(not%20peer%20reviewed)-yellow.svg)](LIMITATIONS.md)

A zero-Mathlib Lean 4.35.0 formalization, an exact-arithmetic verification suite and an AMS-LaTeX preprint with new results that extend Vinciguerra's register-program paper (`arXiv:2609.18692`, an arXiv preprint). No question posed in that paper is resolved. The two-register result characterises, under formal-polynomial cleanliness, which polynomials two-register passive programs with $\mathbb{F}_p$ constants compute. The explicit three-register programs improve the four-register powering exponent bound from $\log_5 4 \approx 0.8614$ to $\log_{13} 8 \approx 0.8107$; this exponent is not proved optimal.

The archived Zenodo `v1.0.1` record ([`10.5281/zenodo.24517199`](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24517199)) and Palomar Registry `v1` entry ([`PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004`](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004&version=1), pinned to verified commit `1a92f47`, deposited prior to the 2026-11-26 audit) carry the earlier title "Optimal Three-Register Exponents"; that word is withdrawn, and release **`v1.1.0`** ([`paper/main.tex`](paper/main.tex) and [`dist/Donahue_2026_catalytic_register_frontiers.pdf`](dist/Donahue_2026_catalytic_register_frontiers.pdf)) carries the corrected title above (see [`ERRATA.md`](ERRATA.md)).

**Author:** Alexander S. Donahue (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA · ORCID [`0009-0006-8168-9648`](https://orcid.org/0009-0006-8168-9648) · `0_0@0thernes.art`)  
**Maintenance status:** active independent research artifact (`v1.1.0`, 2026-11-27) · **Zenodo Concept DOI:** [`10.5281/zenodo.24517198`](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24517198) (prior `v1.0.1`: [`10.5281/zenodo.24517199`](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24517199)) · **Palomar Registry:** [`PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004`](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004&version=1) (`v1`) · **Frozen White Paper:** [`dist/Donahue_2026_catalytic_register_frontiers.pdf`](dist/Donahue_2026_catalytic_register_frontiers.pdf) · **Live Adaptive Forking PWA & Blueprint:** [`0thernes.github.io/catalytic-register-frontiers`](https://0thernes.github.io/catalytic-register-frontiers/) · **SWHID:** [`swh:1:snp:f960eeda6f145e54c0ac52538ace866a16e24085`](https://archive.softwareheritage.org/api/1/snapshot/f960eeda6f145e54c0ac52538ace866a16e24085/)

> **Epistemic Status:** All 22 headline theorems, corollaries, and bi-directional commutative-ring soundness/completeness bridges (`T1`, `T1a`–`T1e`, `T1s`, `T1es`, `T1sc`, `T1esc`, `T2`, `T2b`, `T3a`–`T3i` — including 4-register passive powering for all $N \ge 1$ over rings where $D_8$, $12!$ and $(\lfloor\log_{13} N\rfloor+1)!$ are invertible, and its coordinatewise form over $R^n$ (`T3i`), `T4` — including machine-checked `CatOp.usesOnly` containment within $\le k + 2$ designated registers, a conjunct added in commit `1a92f47`, after the `v1.0.1` tag) plus concrete `0 ≠ 1` non-vacuity witnesses (`NonVacuity`, including bivariate `FPS (FPS (ModP 5))` / `FPS (FPS GF4)` for `T1sc`/`T1esc` and product ring `Fin 3 → ModP 13` for `T3i`) are machine-checked from first principles in **zero-Mathlib Lean 4.35.0** across **14 core module files** (8,930 lines, max 1,511 lines; plus standalone Palomar contract files `PalomarChallenge.lean` [283 lines] and `PalomarSolution.lean`) and **5 distinct kernel implementations across 6 locally reproducible runs** (`lean`, `leanchecker`, `leanchecker-paranoid`, `con-leche --verified`, `con-ron --verified`, `nanoda_bin 0.4.19`) with 0 forbidden tokens and 0 linter warnings. (On Windows, the bundled `lean4lean.exe` fails locally with an upstream `.olean` header mismatch and is excluded from the completed local kernel count; see [`results/six_kernel_audit.txt`](results/six_kernel_audit.txt).) All 8/8 companion SAT UNSAT proofs are archived as ASCII LRAT certificates (`results/sat_certs/`), independently verified (`scripts/verify_lrat.py`), and cross-checked against both brute-force enumeration and a second independent CNF encoder (`tests/test_all.py`). This preprint has **not** undergone external peer review; confirmed archival identifiers are Zenodo Concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.24517198` (prior `v1.0.1`: `10.5281/zenodo.24517199`), Palomar Registry `PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004` (`v1`, commit `1a92f47`), Software Heritage SWHID `swh:1:snp:f960eeda6f145e54c0ac52538ace866a16e24085`, and ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648` (arXiv and HAL IDs are not yet assigned). See [`CLAIMS.md`](CLAIMS.md) and [`LIMITATIONS.md`](LIMITATIONS.md).

### Scope of the claims (2026-11-26 statement audit)

An independent statement audit ([log](https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md)) found the following, and this README follows it:

- **What Lean proves.** `T1` is an exact iff in a stated model: "cleanly computes" means equality of formal polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_p[R, x]$, with program constants in $\mathbb{F}_p$. `T1s` and `T1sc` (`T1es`, `T1esc`, formalized in Pass 22 via zero-Mathlib formal power series $\mathbb{F}_p[[U]][[X]]$) prove the exact equivalence ($\Leftrightarrow$) between formal cleanliness and clean execution over every commutative ring of characteristic $p$ (every commutative $\mathbb{F}_4$-algebra), yielding a direct literal-ring Theorem `T1` (`rp_pass_two_literal_ring_iff`). It is still not a statement about pointwise functions on $\mathbb{F}_p$ alone, where $x^p = x$; for example $x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is computed as a function with one input access, although `T1b` excludes the formal polynomial $x^3$. `T3a`–`T3d`, `T3g` are five explicit programs; `T3f` is an inequality between integers about the formula $\log_{2t-3} t$ and contains no register program.
- **What is not proved.** No upper bound on what three-register programs can achieve, so neither $\log_{13} 8$ nor any other three-register exponent is proved optimal. If $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_3(4) \ge 7$, the exponent $\log_7 4 \approx 0.7124$ would be smaller. No lower bound for `T4`.
- **Relation to Vinciguerra.** Section 6 of `arXiv:2609.18692` asks whether $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}(4) > 2r-1$ and whether additional input accesses drastically increase $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}$. The first question is not addressed here. On the second, `T3a`–`T3g` give lower bounds $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_3(t) \ge 2t-3$ for $t = 5,\dots,9$ only; the question stays open. The positive-characteristic question studied in `T1` is this repository's own extension of Vinciguerra's Theorem 3.5, which is stated for characteristic 0.
- **Prior work for `T4`.** `T4` is the classical four-step clean-product recursion applied in a balanced tree. Ben-Or and Cleve (SIAM J. Comput. 21(1), 1992, [`doi:10.1137/0221006`](https://doi.org/10.1137/0221006)) already compute every polynomial-size formula over an arbitrary ring with three registers in a neighbouring instruction set, and report earlier methods that use logarithmically many registers.

---

|---|---|---|---|

| `T2`, `T2b` (`BilinInstr`, `DistinctBilinInstr`) | Strictly bilinear & distinct-operand Def. 2.2 | `F2 = ModP 2` ($0 \neq 1$), $k = 2$, $x = 1$ | Odd characteristics |
| `T3a`–`T3i` (`Pass3InstrR`, `Pass4Instr`, `instCRingFinFun`, `prog5_x7`..`prog9_x15`, integer minimiser $t=8$ of $\log_{2t-3} t$, 4-reg powering & coordinatewise powering over $R^n$) | Vinciguerra (`arXiv:2609.18692`), Def. 2.2, Cor. 4.3.1, Cor. 5.1.1; Alekseev et al. (MFCS 2025), composition lemma (cited as Lemma 8 in `arXiv:2609.18692`; numbered Lemma 2.1 in `arXiv:2504.17412v1`) | `ModP 5, 7, 11, 13` ($0 \neq 1$) with explicit $D_5^{-1}\!\dots D_9^{-1}$, $12!^{-1}$, $6!^{-1}$ | Optimality of any 3-register exponent; bad primes dividing $D_t$ or $(\ell+1)!$; uniform $t \ge 10$; upper bounds; bit-space accounting |
| `T4_BalancedMultilinearProduct` (`CatOp`) | Zero-workspace strictly distinct bilinear ops; classical four-step clean-product recursion; Ben-Or and Cleve (1992) for a neighbouring model | `Int` ($0 \neq 1$), $d = 4$, 36 ops, clean restoration | Non-power-of-two $d$ without padding; lower-bound optimality; minimality of the register count |

## Core Mathematical Results

1. **Theorem T1 — Base-$p$ digit-sum characterisation of $\mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, t)$, formal-polynomial cleanliness, $\mathbb{F}_p$ constants** ([`DigitSumDichotomy.lean`](lean/Catalytic/DigitSumDichotomy.lean)):
   For every prime $p$, every budget $t \ge 1$, and every univariate polynomial $f(x) = \sum_{d \ge 0} \alpha_d x^d \in \mathbb{F}_p[x]$, with "cleanly computes" meaning equality of formal polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_p[R, x]$:
   $$f \in \mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, t) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \forall\, d \ge 2 \text{ with } \alpha_d \neq 0,\;\; s_p(d) \le \min(p - 1,\; t - 1).$$
   This is a self-posed extension of Vinciguerra's Theorem 3.5, which is stated for characteristic 0; the source poses no positive-characteristic question. As functions on $\mathbb{F}_p$ the statements do not apply, since $x^p = x$.
   - **T1a:** $x^{p^m} \in \mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, 2)$ for all $m \ge 0$ ($D_{2,\mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2) = +\infty$). This uses the identity $(R+x)^{p^m} - R^{p^m} = x^{p^m}$ and shows that the characteristic-0 lower bounds do not extend to characteristic $p$; it does not contradict the source, whose theorems are stated for characteristic 0.
   - **T1b:** With $\mathbb{F}_2$ constants, no program yields the formal polynomial $x^3$, for any $t \ge 0$ (as a function on $\mathbb{F}_2$, $x^3 = x$).
   - **T1c:** Whenever $s_p(d) \ge p$, no program with $\mathbb{F}_p$ constants yields the formal polynomial $x^d$, for any $t \ge 1$.
   - **T1d:** Large-characteristic analogue of Theorem 3.5: whenever $2 \le d < p$, $x^d \in \mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, t) \iff t \ge d + 1$. Nothing is proved over a field of characteristic 0.
   - **T1e:** With $\mathbb{F}_4$ constants the criterion changes ($x^3$ becomes computable with 4 accesses), so it is not stable under field extension.

2. **Theorem T2 — Two-access programs for $x^{2^k}$ with product-only updates in characteristic 2** ([`BilinearFrobenius.lean`](lean/Catalytic/BilinearFrobenius.lean)):
   Under bilinear updates $R_i \leftarrow R_i + R_j R_\ell$ ($j, \ell \neq i$, passive $R_0$; self-squares $R_j = R_\ell$ allowed, removed in `T2b`), for every $k \ge 1$ and every `Char2CRing` $R$, $x^{2^k}$ is cleanly computed in $k + 1$ registers, $4k - 2$ bilinear ops, and **2 input accesses**. This is repeated squaring with $(a+b)^2 = a^2 + b^2$; no lower bound is proved.

3. **Theorem T3 — Explicit three-register programs and an improved four-register powering exponent bound** ([`ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean`](lean/Catalytic/ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean)):
   Explicit Pascal-row shear loops (a sub-language of the Definition 2.2 instruction set) give $x^7 \in \mathrm{RP}(3, 5)$ ($D_5 = 576$, $\log_7 5 \approx 0.82709$), $x^9 \in \mathrm{RP}(3, 6)$ ($D_6 = 382{,}500{,}000$, $\log_9 6 \approx 0.81546$), $x^{11} \in \mathrm{RP}(3, 7)$ ($\log_{11} 7 \approx 0.81151$), $x^{13} \in \mathrm{RP}(3, 8)$ ($\log_{13} 8 \approx 0.81071$), and $x^{15} \in \mathrm{RP}(3, 9)$ ($\log_{15} 9 \approx 0.81137$), each over rings where $D_t$ is invertible. $\log_{13} 8$ is the smallest exponent among the constructed programs; `T3f` shows that $t = 8$ minimises $\log_{2t-3} t$ over integers $t \ge 4$, which is integer arithmetic, not an optimality theorem for register programs. `T3h` uses `prog8_x13` to improve the exponent of Vinciguerra's Cor. 4.3.1 at four registers from $\log_5 4 \approx 0.86135$ to $\log_{13} 8$. The improvement is in the exponent: with the stated constants, $(104/3)\,N^{0.8107}$ is below $20\,N^{0.8614}$ only for $N$ above about 52,000 (the `prog5_x7` variant $(70/3)\,N^{0.8271}$: above about 90). With five registers the source already has the smaller exponent $\log_7 4 \approx 0.7124$. The streaming bit-space bound (Cor. 5.1.1) and the non-commutative matrix-powering lift via `prog5_x7` (Thm. 5.2, $\log_7 5 \approx 0.82709$) are paper-level arguments, not Lean theorems.

4. **Theorem T4 — Balanced zero-workspace multilinear product (classical construction, formalised)** ([`BalancedProduct.lean`](lean/Catalytic/BalancedProduct.lean)):
   Over any commutative ring $R$, for $d = 2^k$, cleanly computes $x_0 \cdots x_{d-1}$ with zero clean workspace, $\log_2 d + 2$ registers, strictly pairwise-distinct indices, and exact primitive op count $(7d^2 - 4)/3$ (this count includes the $d^2$ input-access instructions). The construction is the four-step telescoping clean-product recursion applied in a balanced tree. Ben-Or and Cleve (1992) give polynomial-length three-register programs for all polynomial-size formulas in a neighbouring instruction set; whether a constant number of registers suffices in the instruction set used here is not settled, and no lower bound is proved. The register-count conjunct is part of the Lean statement from commit `1a92f47` on; at the `v1.0.1` tag it was read off the program definition.

## Quickstart

Prerequisites: **Lean 4.35.0** (`elan`), **Python 3.13**, **Tectonic** (CaDiCaL 2.1.2 is bundled with Lean 4.35.0).

```bash
# 1. Install pinned Python dependencies
python -m venv .venv
# Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate   |   Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.lock.txt

# 2. Run the full end-to-end verification pipeline (Lean + tests + figures + PDF + LRAT + REUSE + SHA-256)
just reproduce
# Or on Windows PowerShell without `just`:
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/run_all.ps1 -Task all
# Or on Linux/macOS without `just`:
bash scripts/run_all.sh all
```

Expected result: 19/19 default Lean jobs built with 0 warnings, `leanchecker --fresh`, `leanchecker-paranoid`, `con-leche`, and `con-ron` exit 0, all 35 `pytest` / Hypothesis / mutant / differential-SAT / LRAT / REUSE / SBOM / workflow / schema / SVG / HTML5 / matrix-lift / factorization / JS Adaptive Forking PWA & CLI differential / Build Standard v1.2.0 & Playbook v1.3 consistency tests PASS, 3 deterministic PDFs generated, 0-warning Tectonic PDF compile, 100% `MANIFEST.sha256` verification, and DigiCert RFC 3161 `Verification: OK` (re-sealed cleanly on `main` after the 2026-11-26 statement audit `2a159ce`/`530bf12` and Passes 20–22; see [`ERRATA.md`](ERRATA.md)).

### Universal Zero-Dependency Adaptive Forking CLI (Any Device with Node.js)
```bash
# Accepts --flag=val, --flag val, positional args, selfcheck, CSV horizon, AND raw --stdin piping:
node docs/catalytic-engine.js selfcheck
node docs/catalytic-engine.js plan    --N=169 --p=1009
echo "LiveRAM" | node docs/catalytic-engine.js vault --stdin 91 1009
node docs/catalytic-engine.js stream  "imu_a imu_a imu_b imu_c imu_a" 20 1009
node docs/catalytic-engine.js horizon 137 scalar --csv
node docs/catalytic-engine.js verify  catalytic-proof-*.json
node docs/catalytic-engine.js bench
# Or via just: just adaptive selfcheck
```

## Usage and Examples

### Common Path — Verify Lean Proofs & Run Exact Test Suite
```bash
cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean && lake env leanchecker-paranoid Solution
cd .. && pytest -v tests/test_all.py
```

### Advanced Path — Export Proof Stream to External Kernels & Audit Repository
```bash
cd lean
lake env leanexport Solution -- Catalytic.Solution.prove_all_catalytic_theorems Catalytic.NonVacuity.nonvac_all_hypotheses > /tmp/sol.ndjson
lake env con-leche --verified /tmp/sol.ndjson
lake env con-ron --verified /tmp/sol.ndjson
cd ..
python scripts/check_citations.py --offline
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/Audit-Repo.ps1 -Path .
```

### Negative / Failure Path — Verifying Impossibility & Mutant Rejection
```bash
# Run the dedicated negative, hygiene, & mutant-killing tests (confirms x^3 over F_2 fails and corrupted certificates are rejected)
pytest -v tests/test_all.py -k "mutant or hygiene or bruteforce"
```

# Machine-Auditable Claims Ledger (`CLAIMS.md`)

Every scientific claim in `catalytic-register-frontiers` is assigned an explicit epistemic tier and an explicit refutation condition (Build Standard B04, B42):

- **`TIER-1 (Lean 4.35 Multi-Kernel)`**: Formally verified from first principles in `lean/Solution.lean` + `lean/Catalytic/NonVacuity.lean` (zero Mathlib, zero forbidden tokens, strict core linters clean, axioms $\subseteq \{\text{propext}, \text{Classical.choice}, \text{Quot.sound}\}$, 6 passing kernel runs across 5 implementations).
- **`TIER-2 (Exact-Arithmetic / SAT-Certified)`**: 100% exact integer, rational (`fractions.Fraction`), finite-field ($\mathbb{F}_p$, $\mathbb{F}_4$), or CaDiCaL 2.1.2 SAT/UNSAT computation verified by `pytest`, Hypothesis property tests, mutant checks, and brute-force SAT encoder equivalence tests.
- **`TIER-3 (Paper-Level Reduction)`**: Standard mathematical deduction combining our Tier-1 theorems (`T3a`, `T3d`, `T3h`, `T3i`) with published reductions in Vinciguerra (`arXiv:2609.18692`, Corollary 5.1.1 bit-space accounting, §4.4, and Theorem 5.2).
- **`TIER-4 (Open Frontier)`**: Explicitly unresolved conjecture or research question.

## Tier-1 Machine-Checked Lean 4.35 Theorems

Scope notes (2026-11-26 statement audit, [log](https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md), plus Pass 22 formal completeness upgrade): in `T1`–`T1e`, "cleanly computes" means equality of formal polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_p[R, x]$ (or $\mathbb{F}_4[R, x]$) with program constants in that field. `T1s`/`T1sc` and `T1es`/`T1esc` (`Pass2Soundness.lean`, via zero-Mathlib bivariate formal power series `FPS (FPS R)`) now prove the exact equivalence ($\Leftrightarrow$) between formal cleanliness and clean literal execution over every commutative ring of characteristic $p$ (every commutative $\mathbb{F}_4$-algebra), yielding a direct literal-ring Theorem `T1` (`rp_pass_two_literal_ring_iff`). As pointwise functions on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$ alone, the statements still do not apply, since $x^p = x$. No upper bound for three-register programs is proved, and no three-register exponent is claimed optimal. No question posed in Vinciguerra (`arXiv:2609.18692`) is resolved.

## Tier-3 Paper-Level Reductions

- **`R1` (Now Tier-1 `T3h`):** Four-register passive powering for all $N \ge 1$ (`Cor. 5.2`), over rings where the stated constants are invertible, is machine-checked in Lean 4.35 (`lean/Catalytic/FourRegisterPowering.lean`, `T3h_FourRegPowering`) across 5 distinct kernel implementations (6 runs). The real-exponent and big-O forms are paper-level conversions of the integer bound.
- **`R2` (Catalytic streaming frequency moments $F_D(\sigma)$ — coordinatewise powering bound in Tier-1 `T3i`; stream model and bit-space accounting Tier-3):** The algebraic vector powering bound ($F_D(\mathbf{f}) = \sum_{i<n} f_i^D$ cleanly computed over the product ring `Fin n → R` in $< \frac{104}{3} \cdot 8^\ell \le \frac{8}{3} \cdot 13 D^{\log_{13} 8}$ passes for every $n$ and $D \ge 1$) is now **machine-checked in Lean 4.35** (`T3i_StreamingFrequencyMoment`, `FourRegisterPowering.lean`). The remaining bit-space accounting over $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ with $p > \max(12, m^D, \lfloor\log_{13} D\rfloor + 1)$ and $p \nmid D_8$ — $O(n D \log(m+1))$ catalytic bits and $O(D \log(m+1) + \log n + \log D)$ regular workspace bits (matching Corollary 5.1.1 of `arXiv:2609.18692`) — stays Tier-3.
- **`R3` (Non-commutative matrix powering $A^N$):** Lifting `T3a` (`prog5_x7`, shear degree $d = 2$) via Vinciguerra §4.4's $\ell_A(z)$ homogeneous lift cleanly computes $A^N$ for $A \in M_m(\mathbb{F}_p)$ ($p > \max(7, \lfloor \log_7 N \rfloor + 1)$) using at most $\frac{10}{3} \cdot 7 \cdot N^{\log_7 5} = O(N^{0.82709})$ recursive matrix calls and the **exact** $r=3$ scalar register count $2m^2 + \binom{m^2+2}{2} - 1 = 3m^2 + \binom{m^2+1}{2}$ (zero extra scalar registers vs. Theorem 5.2 of `arXiv:2609.18692`). Lifting `T3d` (`prog8_x13`, shear degree $d = 6$, $p > \max(13, \lfloor \log_{13} N \rfloor + 1)$, $p \nmid D_8$) achieves $O(N^{0.81072})$ calls using $3m^2 + \binom{m^2+5}{6} = \Theta(m^{12})$ scalar registers. (Concrete non-commutative instances — literal $\mu_7(\texttt{prog5\_x7})$ on $M_2(\mathbb{F}_{11})$ with non-commuting catalytic $(O_0, u_0(z), v_0(z))$, single-catalyst $\mu_2$-lifted and 2-factor Cook–Mertz $A^{23}$ on $M_2(\mathbb{F}_{11})$ / $M_3(\mathbb{F}_{11})$, and the scalar-register identity for $m = 1..20$ — are independently verified in exact modular arithmetic by `test_pass9_cor54_matrix_lift_and_blueprint_integrity` in `tests/test_all.py`; the general symbolic matrix-lift theorem stays Tier-3.)

## What Would Prove Us Wrong (Refutation & Falsification Criteria — Build Standard B42)

Every claim in this repository is explicitly falsifiable:

1. **Refuting Formal Correctness (`T1`–`T4`, `NONVAC`):** Any of: (a) a clean rebuild of `lean/` failing or emitting any axiom outside `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}`; (b) any of the 5 distinct kernel implementations across 6 runs (`lean`, `leanchecker`, `leanchecker-paranoid`, `con-leche`, `con-ron`, `nanoda_bin`) rejecting the exported proof stream; or (c) any mismatch between `lean/Challenge.lean` definitions and Vinciguerra (`arXiv:2609.18692`, Def. 2.2) documented in `docs/statement-fidelity.md`.
2. **Refuting `T1` (Digit-Sum Dichotomy):** Exhibiting a single prime $p$, budget $t \ge 1$, and passive 2-register program with $\mathbb{F}_p$ constants cleanly computing, as an identity of formal polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_p[R, x]$, a monomial $x^d$ ($d \ge 2$) with $s_p(d) > \min(p-1, t-1)$ — e.g., any clean 2-register program computing $x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_2[x]$ in any number of calls $t$.
3. **Refuting `T2` or `T4`:** Exhibiting an input/catalytic state where `frobBilinProg` (over a `Char2CRing`) or `balancedProdProg` (over a `CRing`) fails to restore a single catalytic register or violates passive/strictly-distinct operand rules, or fails Hypothesis randomized testing in `tests/test_all.py`.
4. **Refuting `T3` (3-Register Exponent Improvement):** Finding a single input/catalyst triple $(x, u, v)$ where `prog5_x7`..`prog8_x13` fails to compute $O + D_t x^{2t-3}$ cleanly, or finding a good prime $p \nmid D_t$ where reduction modulo $p$ fails.
5. **Refuting `E5` (SAT Companion Audit):** Exhibiting a valid 2-AND unrestricted XAG circuit over $\mathbb{F}_2$ computing $\mathbb{F}_4$ multiplication, the orthogonal bent pair, or any of the 6 UNSAT $(n=4, m=3)$ maps — or finding a single input where our CNF encoder disagrees with brute-force ground truth.
6. **Refuting Novelty:** Citing any peer-reviewed paper or preprint predating 2026-11-23 that already proved Theorem `T1` (exact base-$p$ digit-sum IFF for $\mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_p}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, t)$) or `T3d` ($x^{13} \in \mathrm{RP}_K^{\mathrm{pass}}(3, 8)$ achieving $\log_{13} 8$). If found, we will immediately log it in `ERRATA.md` and reframe to formalization/rediscovery. `T4` is already classified as a formalisation of a classical construction: Ben-Or and Cleve (SIAM J. Comput. 21(1), 1992, `doi:10.1137/0221006`) compute polynomial-size formulas with three registers in a neighbouring instruction set.

## Tier-4 Open Frontiers (Explicitly Unresolved)

- **`O1`**: Uniform proof of $D_{3,\mathbb{Q}}^{\mathrm{pass}}(t) = 2t - 3$ for all $t \ge 4$ (and matching upper bounds for $r \ge 3$).
- **`O2`**: Whether non-triangular or multi-stage $r = 4$ loops can reach $N \ge 10$ at $t=5$ or $N \ge 13$ at $t=6$ to beat Vinciguerra's $r=4$ exponent $\log_7 4 \approx 0.71241$.
- **`O3`**: General closed-form combinatorial characterization of $\mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_{p^e}}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, t)$ over non-prime extension fields ($e \ge 2$).
- **`O4`**: The open question of Boyar and Find (TCS 720, 2018) and Morse's $n = 5$ binary polynomial multiplication program (`arXiv:2608.30238`).
- **`O5`**: Both questions of Vinciguerra (`arXiv:2609.18692`, Sec. 6): whether $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}(4) > 2r - 1$, and whether additional input accesses drastically increase $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}$. `T3a`–`T3g` give only the lower bounds $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_3(t) \ge 2t - 3$ for $t = 5, \dots, 9$; optimality of any three-register exponent is open.

---

## FILE: LIMITATIONS.md

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0 -->
# Limitations, Epistemic Scope, and Negative Findings (`LIMITATIONS.md`)

This document explicitly states what `catalytic-register-frontiers` **does not** prove, documents negative computational findings, and classifies discovered defects using the Build Standard v1.2.0 taxonomy `{bug, error, issue, problem, concern, dilemma, conflict, gap, hole, blindspot}`.

## 1. Explicit Scope Boundaries

1. **Prime fields vs. extension fields (Theorems T1 & T1e):**
   Theorem `T1` (`rp_pass_two_iff`) holds for every **prime field** $\mathbb{F}_p$, with program constants in $\mathbb{F}_p$ and formal-polynomial cleanliness (item 2). It does **not** hold verbatim for non-prime finite fields $\mathbb{F}_{p^e}$ ($e \ge 2$): Theorem `T1e` (`ExtensionFieldSeparation.lean`) now formally proves in Lean 4.35 that over $\mathbb{F}_4$, $x^5 \in \mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_4}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, 3)$ and $x^3 \in \mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_4}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, 4)$ while $x^7 \notin \mathrm{RP}_{\mathbb{F}_4}^{\mathrm{pass}}(2, t)$ for all $t$. A general closed-form criterion for arbitrary $\mathbb{F}_{p^e}$ remains open (`O3`).
2. **Formal polynomial cleanliness vs. functional evaluation:**
   Vinciguerra's Definition 2.2 is functional: from any initial state the program ends with $R_i \leftarrow R_i + f_i(x)$. This repository uses the Definition 2.2 instruction set with formal polynomial identity in $R[O, R_1, \dots, R_{r-1}, x]$. `T1s`/`T1sc` (and `T1es`/`T1esc` for $\mathbb{F}_4$) now formally prove in Lean 4.35 (`Pass2Soundness.lean`, via zero-Mathlib bivariate formal power series `FPS (FPS R)`) the exact equivalence ($\Leftrightarrow$) between formal cleanliness and literal clean execution over every commutative ring of characteristic $p$ (yielding `rp_pass_two_literal_ring_iff` directly on `Pass2Prog.execRing`). Over $\mathbb{F}_p$ alone, however, functional (pointwise) evaluation still differs from formal-polynomial / universal-ring cleanliness because $x^p = x$ as functions: the one-access program $O \mathrel{+}= x$ maps $(o, u)$ to $(o + x^3, u)$ for all $o, u, x \in \mathbb{F}_2$, while `T1b` says that no program yields the formal polynomial $x^3$ with $\mathbb{F}_2$ constants. None of the `T1` statements is a claim about pointwise functions on a single finite field.
3. **Finite family ($t \in \{5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$) vs. all $t \ge 4$ (Theorem T3):**
   Our Lean 4.35 proofs establish all five explicit programs $x^7 \in \mathrm{RP}_K^{\mathrm{pass}}(3, 5)$ (`T3a`), $x^9 \in \mathrm{RP}_K^{\mathrm{pass}}(3, 6)$ (`T3b`), $x^{11} \in \mathrm{RP}_K^{\mathrm{pass}}(3, 7)$ (`T3c`), $x^{13} \in \mathrm{RP}_K^{\mathrm{pass}}(3, 8)$ (`T3d`), and $x^{15} \in \mathrm{RP}_K^{\mathrm{pass}}(3, 9)$ (`T3g`), plus the integer fact that $t = 8$ minimises $\log_{2t-3} t$ over integers $t \ge 4$ (`T3f`; no register program occurs in that statement). These are lower bounds $D_{3}^{\mathrm{pass}}(t) \ge 2t - 3$ for $t = 5, \dots, 9$. No upper bound on $D_{3}^{\mathrm{pass}}(t)$ is proved, so no three-register exponent, $\log_{13} 8$ included, is shown to be optimal: if $D_{3}^{\mathrm{pass}}(4) \ge 7$, the exponent $\log_7 4 \approx 0.7124$ would be smaller. Programs for $t \ge 10$, equality $D_{3,\mathbb{Q}}^{\mathrm{pass}}(t) = 2t - 3$ and all upper bounds remain open (`O1`).
4. **Bad-prime & finite-characteristic restrictions for $t = 6, 7, 8$ and `T3h`:**
   While `prog5_x7` ($\epsilon = 0.827087$) avoids only $\{2, 3\}$ (matching Vinciguerra's $t = 4$ characteristic requirement!), `prog6_x9` avoids $\{2, 3, 5, 17\}$, and `prog7_x11` / `prog8_x13` avoid two larger primes arising from clearing denominators (`538423, 2512452073` and `137, 1602207194491`). Furthermore, in 4-register passive powering (`T3h`, Corollary 5.2), inverting the digit-program and Cook–Mertz finite-difference denominators $(\delta - 1)!$ and $(\lfloor\log_\delta N\rfloor + 1)!$ requires characteristic $0$ or prime characteristic $p > \max(12, \lfloor\log_{13} N\rfloor + 1)$ with $p \nmid D_8$ (for `prog8_x13`) / $p > \max(6, \lfloor\log_7 N\rfloor + 1)$ (for `prog5_x7`). All constructions hold unconditionally in characteristic $0$.
5. **No $r = 4$ exponent improvement:**
   Our exact modular linear-algebra audit over $r = 4$ triangular closed loops (reproduced deterministically via `verify_r4_triangular_frontier()` in `experiments/exp2_three_register_breakthrough.py`, $d_1 = 2, d_2 = 4$ over $\mathbb{F}_{10^9+7}$) reaches $N = 9$ at $t=5$ ($\epsilon = 0.73249$, $N = 10$ unsolvable) and $N = 11$ at $t=6$ ($\epsilon = 0.74722$, $N = 12$ unsolvable). Because degree grew as $2t - 1$ rather than faster, this family did **not** beat Vinciguerra's $r = 4, t = 4$ baseline $N = 7$ ($\log_7 4 \approx 0.71241$).
6. **Boyar–Find open question & SAT certificate boundary:**
   `exp4_boolean_mc_companion.py` provides supporting SAT-certified evidence (0 counterexamples across sampled degree-3 cancellations and hard $n = 4$ maps) and does **not** prove or refute Boyar–Find (TCS 720, 2018) or Morse's $n = 5$ conjecture (`arXiv:2608.30238`). Our CNF encoder is verified against an independent exhaustive brute-force enumerator on all 16 $n=2$ functions ($k=0, 1$) and canonical $n=3$ benchmarks in `tests/test_all.py`, AND all **8/8** CaDiCaL 2.1.2 DIMACS `.cnf` + ASCII `.lrat` UNSAT certificates (`results/sat_certs/`, 18,932 total verified steps) are archived and independently verified step-by-step by `scripts/verify_lrat.py` (including mutant-rejection tests in `tests/test_all.py`). They have **not** yet been replayed through CakeML's formally verified `cake_lpr` binary (external binary not installed locally — classified as `problem`; no Tier-1 Lean theorem depends on SAT).
7. **Peer-review, Windows tooling, & archival provenance status:**
   This manuscript has **not** undergone external peer review or external second-machine human reproduction (`REPLICATION.md`). On Windows, `lean4lean.exe` bundled in Lean 4.35.0 fails locally with an upstream `.olean` header-version mismatch (`incompatible header`, classified as `problem`), and `lake check --paranoid` requires POSIX `bwrap`; accordingly, `lean4lean` is omitted from the completed local kernel count (`results/six_kernel_audit.txt`). Correctness of all Tier-1 theorems is certified locally across **5 distinct Lean 4.35 kernel implementations in 6 runs** (`lean`, `leanchecker`, `leanchecker-paranoid`, `con-leche --verified`, `con-ron --verified`, `nanoda_bin 0.4.19`). **Confirmed live archival identifiers:** GitHub (`0thernes/catalytic-register-frontiers`, live CI & SLSA releases `v1.0.0`/`v1.0.1`/`v1.1.0`), GitHub Pages Blueprint (`https://0thernes.github.io/catalytic-register-frontiers/`), Zenodo Concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.24517198` (prior `v1.0.1` Version DOI `10.5281/zenodo.24517199`), Palomar Registry `PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004` (`v1`, pinned to verified commit `1a92f47`, `https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000004&version=1`; carries pre-audit title), Software Heritage snapshot `swh:1:snp:f960eeda6f145e54c0ac52538ace866a16e24085`, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, and `0thernes-research-archive` record `0TH-2026-010`. **Planned deposits not yet assigned:** arXiv ID, HAL ID, and Bitcoin block confirmation for `provenance/MANIFEST.sha256.ots` (`ROADMAP.md`).
8. **Relation to the cited literature (2026-11-26 statement audit):**
   No question posed in Vinciguerra (`arXiv:2609.18692`, a v1 arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed) is resolved. Its Section 6 asks whether $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}(4) > 2r - 1$ (not addressed here) and whether additional input accesses drastically increase $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}$ (only the lower bounds of item 3 are given). The two-register positive-characteristic question of `T1` is this repository's own; the source's Section 3 is stated for characteristic 0, and `T1d` is a large-characteristic analogue of its Theorem 3.5, not a statement over a characteristic-0 field. `T4` is the classical four-step clean-product recursion in a balanced tree; Ben-Or and Cleve (SIAM J. Comput. 21(1), 1992, `doi:10.1137/0221006`) already compute polynomial-size formulas over arbitrary rings with three registers in a neighbouring instruction set, and no lower bound for `T4` is proved. The improvement of `T3h` over Corollary 4.3.1 is in the exponent; with the stated constants the new bound is the smaller one only for $N$ above about 52,000 (base-7 variant: above about 90). The register-count conjunct of `T4` (`CatOp.usesOnly`, $\le k + 2$ registers) is part of the Lean statement from commit `1a92f47` on; at the `v1.0.1` tag it was read off the program definition. Audit log: <https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md>.

## 2. Classified Engineering & Discovery Log

| Type | Observation | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `conflict` | Legacy notes cited `0thernes LLC` and MIT vs. Nov 2026 Playbook audit (no LLC legally formed; Apache-2.0 + CC-BY-4.0). | Resolved in `docs/adr/0002-epistemic-scope-and-identity.md`: author `Alexander S. Donahue` (independent researcher), Apache-2.0 + CC-BY-4.0. |
| `bug` | `Poly3.add` initially used well-founded recursion, preventing Lean kernel `rfl` reduction on `exec3Poly`. | Rewrote `Poly3.add` via nested structural recursion (`Poly3.addAux`), enabling pure kernel `rfl` across all 5 distinct kernel implementations. |
| `bug` | PowerShell `Out-File -Encoding ascii` wrapped/CRLF-encoded `leanexport` lines, causing `nanoda_bin` parser panic. | Wrote raw LF binary stream via Python `subprocess`; `nanoda_bin 0.4.19` checks all 3,644 exported `Solution` declarations (and 3,502 `PalomarSolution` declarations) cleanly with exit 0. |
| `issue` | Trial-division prime factoring stalled on $t=9$'s 15-digit cofactor (`638970634117961`). | Upgraded `factor_primes` in `exp2` to Miller–Rabin + Pollard-Rho; runtime dropped to < 1 s. |
| `problem` | $t=5$ with `deg_w = 3` failed to reach $N = 7$, initially looking like an anomaly. | Discovered `deg_w = 2` unlocks $x^7$ at $t=5$ with tiny `D = 576` and bad primes ONLY `{2, 3}`! |
| `dilemma` | Balancing Lean `prog8_x13` (`maxRecDepth 4096`) and `prog9_x15` (`maxRecDepth 8192`) kernel reduction depth against external checker performance. | Verified all 5 distinct local kernel implementations (6 runs: `lean`, `leanchecker`, `leanchecker-paranoid`, `con-leche`, `con-ron`, `nanoda_bin`) accept both in seconds with zero `native_decide`. |

## FILE: REPLICATION.md

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0 -->
# Clean-Room Replication Guide (`REPLICATION.md`)

Every Lean 4.35 formal proof, non-vacuity witness, exact-arithmetic experiment, `pytest` / Hypothesis / mutant / SAT-equivalence test, deterministic vector PDF figure, and frozen AMS-LaTeX manuscript in `catalytic-register-frontiers` reproduces end-to-end from scratch.

## Prerequisites

- **Lean 4.35.0** via `elan` (`leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`, pinned in `lean/lean-toolchain`). Zero Mathlib dependency; builds fully offline once the toolchain is installed.
- **Python 3.13** with pinned packages in `requirements.lock.txt` (`pytest==9.2.0`, `hypothesis==6.170.17`, `matplotlib==3.11.2`, `numpy==2.5.5`, `scipy==1.18.1`, `ruff==0.17.6`, `mypy==2.4.1`).
- **CaDiCaL 2.1.2** (bundled with Lean 4.35.0 at `<toolchain>/bin/cadical[.exe]`, or set `CADICAL_BIN`).
- **Tectonic** (`tectonic -X compile`) for compiling `paper/main.tex`.

## 1. One-Command Verification (Windows PowerShell, Linux/macOS Bash, or `just`)

> **Bracket-Path Safety Note:** On Windows paths containing `[...]`, always pass `-LiteralPath` to PowerShell file cmdlets and run `pytest` repo-relative (`tests/test_all.py`).

```bash
# Windows PowerShell
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/run_all.ps1 -Task all

# Linux / macOS POSIX shell
bash scripts/run_all.sh all

# Cross-platform via justfile
just reproduce
```

Individual stages: `lean`, `experiments`, `tests`, `figures`, `paper`, `audit` (verifies 8/8 LRAT proofs, 100% REUSE/SPDX, offline citations, and `MANIFEST.sha256`).

## 2. Step-by-Step Verification (Linux / macOS / CI)

### A. Clean-from-Scratch Lean 4.35 Multi-Kernel Audit

```bash
cd lean
rm -rf .lake
lake build
lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean
lake env leanchecker --fresh Solution
lake env leanchecker-paranoid Solution

# Export self-contained LF NDJSON stream for external verified kernels
lake env leanexport Solution -- \
  Catalytic.Solution.prove_all_catalytic_theorems \
  Catalytic.NonVacuity.nonvac_all_hypotheses > /tmp/catalytic_solution.ndjson
lake env con-leche --verified /tmp/catalytic_solution.ndjson
lake env con-ron --verified /tmp/catalytic_solution.ndjson

# On Linux (with bwrap installed), run Lean 4.35's bundled sandboxed multi-kernel checker:
lake check --paranoid
```

### B. Exact-Arithmetic Experiments, Pytest, Hypothesis, & Linters

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.lock.txt

python experiments/exp1_digit_sum_dichotomy.py
python experiments/exp2_three_register_breakthrough.py
python experiments/exp3_bilinear_and_balanced.py
python experiments/exp4_boolean_mc_companion.py

pytest -v tests/test_all.py
ruff check experiments scripts tests
mypy experiments scripts tests
python scripts/check_citations.py --offline
```

### C. Deterministic Vector Figures & AMS-LaTeX Manuscript

```bash
python scripts/make_figures.py
cd paper
mkdir -p build
tectonic -X compile main.tex --outdir build --keep-intermediates
```

### D. Standalone arXiv Tarball Clean-Room Compilation Test

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/arxiv_check
tar -xzf dist/arxiv_submission.tar.gz -C /tmp/arxiv_check
cd /tmp/arxiv_check
tectonic -X compile main.tex --outdir out
```

### E. Cryptographic Provenance & Build Standard Audit

```bash
sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/Audit-Repo.ps1 -Path .
```

## 2026-11-26 statement audit

An independent statement audit of this repository was carried out on 2026-11-26. Audit log: <https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md>. The public claim documents (`README.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `LIMITATIONS.md`, `CITATION.cff`, `lean/formalization.yaml`, `docs/*.md`, `docs/index.html`, `docs/media/social-preview.svg`) were corrected in commits `2a159ce` and `530bf12`. In Pass 20 (immediately following `530bf12`), all 14 `paper/main.tex`, `paper/references.bib`, and `paper/arxiv_metadata.txt` items below were resolved on `main` and the PDF, arXiv tarball, and `MANIFEST.sha256` + RFC 3161 timestamp were rebuilt and re-sealed. The frozen Zenodo `v1.0.1` record and the Lean files (docstrings/identifiers listed below) were not modified in this pass. Line numbers below refer to the files on `main` at commit `646443c`.

### Errors in the paper (`paper/main.tex`, `paper/references.bib`, frozen PDF `dist/Donahue_2026_catalytic_register_frontiers.pdf`)

| Where | What is wrong | Correction | Affects a theorem statement? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paper/main.tex:32` (title); same title in `.zenodo.json`, the Zenodo `v1.0.1` record and the frozen PDF | "Optimal Three-Register Exponents". No upper bound on what three-register programs can achieve is proved. | "Prime-Field Digit-Sum Dichotomy and Improved Three-Register Powering Exponents in Passive Catalytic Register Programs". | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:52` (abstract) | "We resolve two structural questions left open by Vinciguerra". Section 6 of `arXiv:2609.18692` poses neither question studied here. It asks whether $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}(4) > 2r-1$ and whether additional input accesses drastically increase $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}$; both stay open. | "We prove new results extending Vinciguerra's analysis; no question posed there is resolved." | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:92–98` (introduction, (Q1)/(Q2)) | "leaving open two sharp structural questions" attributes the paper's own (Q1), (Q2) to the source; "we answer both (Q1) ... and (Q2)". (Q2) receives lower bounds $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_3(t) \ge 2t-3$ for $t = 5,\dots,9$ only. | "which suggests two questions that we study here"; quote Section 6 of the source verbatim; say that (Q1) is answered for $r = 2$ in the formal-polynomial model and that (Q2) receives lower bounds only. | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:88` | "$D_{2,K}^{\mathrm{pass}}(t) = t - 1$ for every $t \ge 1$ ([Theorem 3.5])". The source states Theorem 3.5 for every $t \ge 2$ (and Theorem 3.2 gives $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_{r,K}(1) = 1$). | "for every $t \ge 2$". | Only the quotation of the cited theorem; no result of this paper changes. |
| `paper/main.tex:60`, `:117`; also the corollary list after `:115` | "the char.-0 lower bounds ... collapse in every prime characteristic", "Total collapse of Theorems 3.2, 3.3, and 3.5". The source states these theorems for characteristic 0 only; they are not contradicted. | "the characteristic-0 lower bounds do not extend to characteristic $p$ ($x^{p^m}$ with 2 accesses)". | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:200–210` (Definition of $\mathrm{RP}$ and Remark), `:637` | "formal polynomial-ring cleanliness ... (matching [Vinciguerra2026])". The source's Definition 2.2 is functional (from any initial state the program ends with $R_i \leftarrow R_i + f_i(x)$). Over $\mathbb{F}_p$ the two notions differ: the one-access program $O \mathrel{+}= x$ maps $(o,u)$ to $(o + x^3, u)$ for all $o, u, x \in \mathbb{F}_2$, while Theorem 1.1 (`T1b`) excludes the formal polynomial $x^3$. | "We use the instruction set of [Def. 2.2] with formal-polynomial cleanliness (correctness over every commutative ring of characteristic $p$); this differs from the functional notion of [Def. 2.2] over finite fields." State that program constants lie in $\mathbb{F}_p$, and that the step from literal execution back to the formal predicate is a paper-level argument. | Yes, for how Theorem 1.1 and its corollaries must be read: the model has to be stated in the theorem. The Lean statement `T1_DigitSumDichotomy` is unchanged and already uses the formal model. |
| `paper/main.tex:98`, `:153` and the T4 section | `T4` is called "an optimal balanced zero-workspace bilinear multilinear product" and "a sharp balanced ... construction". No lower bound is proved. The T4 section compares only with a naive linear chain and does not position the result against Ben-Or and Cleve (SIAM J. Comput. 21(1), 54–58, 1992, `doi:10.1137/0221006`), who compute every polynomial-size formula over an arbitrary ring with three registers in a neighbouring instruction set and report earlier methods with logarithmically many registers. | Delete "optimal" and "sharp" for `T4`. Add a related-work paragraph that credits the four-step clean-product recursion, states how the instruction set differs from Ben-Or and Cleve's, and says that whether a constant number of registers suffices in this instruction set is not settled here. | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:131` | "we break Vinciguerra's 4-call powering barrier". The source presents $x^5 \in \mathrm{RP}^{\mathrm{pass}}_K(3,4)$ as a construction, not as a barrier. | "we go beyond the 4-access construction of [Theorem 2.3]". | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:355` (section title), `:408` | "Optimal Three-Register Powering"; `T3f` presented as optimality. `T3f` says only that $t = 8$ minimises $\log_{2t-3} t$ over integers $t \ge 4$. If $D^{\mathrm{pass}}_3(4) \ge 7$, the exponent $\log_7 4 \approx 0.7124$ would be smaller. | "Improved Three-Register Powering"; "$\log_{13} 8$ is the smallest exponent among the constructed programs; optimality among three-register programs is open". | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:482` (Corollary, Four-Register Powering) | The improvement over [Cor. 4.3.1] is in the exponent only; this is not said. | Add: "the $x^{13}$-based bound is below $20\,N^{\log_5 4}$ only for $N$ above about $5.2 \cdot 10^4$ (the $x^7$-based bound: above about 90); with five registers [Cor. 4.3.1] already gives the smaller exponent $\log_7 4$." | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:480`, `:494`, `:626` | Locator "[Lemma~8]{AFM2025}". The composition lemma is numbered Lemma 2.1 in `arXiv:2504.17412v1`; "Lemma 8" is the numbering used when `arXiv:2609.18692` cites it (LIPIcs numbering not checked by the audit). | "Composition Lemma (Lemma 8 in the MFCS version as cited by Vinciguerra; Lemma 2.1 in arXiv:2504.17412v1)", after checking the LIPIcs PDF. | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:577`, `:657` (open problem) | "the long-standing Boyar--Find conjecture". Boyar and Find state an open question; Morse (`arXiv:2608.30238`) calls it "the Boyar--Find question". | "the open question of Boyar and Find". | No. |
| `paper/main.tex:503` (streaming corollary); paper section list | No related-work section; the catalytic streaming baselines that `arXiv:2609.18692` compares with (Kaplan et al.; Becker et al.) are not cited. | Add them and one sentence placing the pass bound on the known pass/space trade-off. | No. |
| `paper/references.bib` (`Lucas1878`) | One DOI (`10.2307/2369308`) is attached to the page range 184–240, 289–321. The Crossref record covers only the instalment starting at p. 184. | Cite that instalment only with this DOI, or list one DOI per instalment. | No. |
| Zenodo record `10.5281/zenodo.24517199` (description; external record, reported by the literature stage of the audit) | Says the preprint answers open questions of Vinciguerra and Morse. | In the next Zenodo version: "new results on passive catalytic register programs extending Vinciguerra (arXiv:2609.18692), with a SAT companion related to Morse (arXiv:2608.30238)". | No. |
| `lean/Challenge.lean` (`T4_BalancedMultilinearProduct`) at the `v1.0.1` tag (`8e4d53e`) | The statement asserted the instruction count, distinct indices and clean execution, but not that only $k + 2$ registers are used; the register count quoted in public summaries was read off the program definition. | Fixed on `main` in commit `1a92f47` (conjuncts `regs.length ≤ k + 2` and `op.usesOnly regs`). Not yet in a tagged release; a new tag is needed before citing the register count as kernel-checked at a release. | Yes (the statement at the tag is weaker than the public claim); fixed on `main`. |

### Known issues in the formal code (docstrings fixed in Pass 21; `T1s`/`T1es` converse resolved in Pass 22; legacy identifiers preserved for Palomar `1a92f47`)

No theorem statement is wrong, and no proof is affected. In **Pass 21**, every overclaiming docstring across `Challenge.lean`, `PalomarChallenge.lean`, `DigitSumDichotomy.lean`, `ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean`, and `FourRegisterPowering.lean` was corrected (comment-only 1-for-1 edits preserving all theorem types, proofs, and line counts). In **Pass 22**, the converse direction of `T1s` and `T1es` was formally machine-checked in `Pass2Soundness.lean` (`T1sc_Pass2RingEquiv`, `T1esc_Pass2GF4Equiv`, and `rp_pass_two_literal_ring_iff`) via zero-Mathlib bivariate formal power series `FPS (FPS R)`. The legacy Lean declaration identifiers (`T3f_GlobalIntegerOptimality`, `T1d_VinciguerraRecovery`, `T3i_StreamingFrequencyMoment`) and module filename (`ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean`) remain intentionally preserved for Palomar `1a92f47` / Comparator backward compatibility until a future major release.

| Where | What is wrong | Correction | Affects a theorem statement? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lean/Challenge.lean:141`; `lean/Catalytic/ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean:496`, `:575` | Docstrings call $\log_{13} 8$ the "optimal 3-register exponent". Not proved. | "the smallest exponent among the constructed programs $t = 4..9$". | No (docstring only). |
| `lean/Challenge.lean:158–161` (`T3f_GlobalIntegerOptimality`); `lean/Catalytic/ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean:629–636` (`exponent_global_integer_optimality`) | Name and docstring "Unconditional Global Integer Optimality" for an inequality between integer powers; no register program occurs in the statement. | Rename, for example `T3f_ArgminOfFamilyExponent`; docstring "t = 8 is the unique integer minimiser of log_(2t−3) t for t ≥ 4". | No (name only). |
| `lean/Catalytic/FourRegisterPowering.lean:1159` | Docstring "Optimal `prog8_x13` 4-Register Passive Powering". | Drop "Optimal". | No. |
| `lean/Catalytic/DigitSumDichotomy.lean:19–22` | Docstring says Vinciguerra's characteristic-0 lower bounds "fail completely in every positive prime characteristic". They are stated for characteristic 0 only. | "the characteristic-0 lower bounds do not extend to characteristic p". | No. |
| `lean/Challenge.lean:43–45` (`T1d_VinciguerraRecovery`) | Docstring "Characteristic-0 Limit Recovering Vinciguerra Theorem 3.5" for a statement over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $d < p$; nothing is proved over a characteristic-0 field. | Rename to a "large-characteristic analogue" of Theorem 3.5. | No. |
| `lean/Challenge.lean:202–209` (`T3i_StreamingFrequencyMoment`) | The statement is `T3h` in the product ring `Fin n → R`; it has no stream, update model or space bound. | Rename to a coordinatewise powering corollary. | No. |
| File name `lean/Catalytic/ThreeRegisterBreakthrough.lean` | "Breakthrough" overstates an improved upper bound for four-register powering. | Rename, for example `ThreeRegisterPowering.lean`, at the next Lean change. | No. |
| `lean/Catalytic/Pass2Soundness.lean` (`T1s`) | Initially only one direction was formalised: formal cleanliness implies correct execution over every characteristic-$p$ commutative ring. The converse (literal clean execution over every characteristic-$p$ ring implies the formal predicate) was not a Lean theorem at `v1.0.1`. | **Resolved in Pass 22** via zero-Mathlib formal power series `FPS (FPS R)` in `Pass2Soundness.lean`: `T1sc_Pass2RingEquiv` (and `T1esc_Pass2GF4Equiv` for $\mathbb{F}_4$) proves the exact bi-implication (`↔`), yielding direct literal-ring Theorem `T1` (`rp_pass_two_literal_ring_iff`); pointwise functions on $\mathbb{F}_p$ alone still differ because $x^p = x$. | No (missing theorem, now formalized on `main`). |
